claim_basis.claim: v2 supervisor verify-control ok; claim, heartbeat and finish recorded in the queue ledger

limits: Read-only research. No OS code change, patch import, build, test, image execution, merge, upstream submission or access-control bypass. No runtime acceptance asserted.
method: Cheapest-first: local pinned published evidence, then live read-only JIRA REST and GitHub REST primaries; external content treated as untrusted; no aggregation inferred as primary fact.
negative_result: No shared root cause is asserted across all three lanes; the only PROVEN shared causal link found is inside the USB3 boot/setup driver-binding lane.
objective: Cluster open issues across the WoW64, FAT/boot-filesystem and USB3 lanes by suspected shared cause, with every member and cause labelled PROVEN or HYPOTHETICAL.

caution: PR 9750 says it was tested in QEMU (qemu-xhci); that is an author claim in a PR body, not an independent reproduction by this research lane.
evidence_quote_9750: ReferenceClassVersion() treats a failed ZwLoadDriver for the class library as success, which leaves ClassLibraryInfo NULL. WdfVersionBindClass() then dereferences it and page-faults. We hit this when usbxhci was loaded as a boot driver during setup and Ucx01000 couldn't load yet (0xc000003a, no filesystem).
evidence_quote_9865: the xHCI controller and the USB3 root hub are in neither place, so setup binds no driver to them. On a machine whose only USB controller is xHCI, setup has no USB at all: no install media and no keyboard.
interpretation: The causal co-occurrence and both failure modes are stated in the primary PR bodies and are therefore PROVEN as author-reported scenarios. They are not proven to be a single defect: each PR changes a different file and neither is merged. Runtime acceptance is NOT established by this clustering.
label: PROVEN

members.summary: Create a driver to support USB xHCI controllers
0x7B INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE booting from USB on Skylake HM170 (xHCI-only, ASUS GL552VW)

members.title: [BOOTDATA] Install the USB3 stack during setup
[WDFLDR] Fail WdfVersionBindClass if the class library never loaded

shared_cause: Setup-time USB3 driver binding depends on two sequential conditions: install metadata must map the xHCI/root-hub hardware IDs, and the WDF class library must load before WdfVersionBindClass dereferences ClassLibraryInfo. PR 9750's own body states that usbxhci loaded as a boot driver during setup while Ucx01000 could not load yet (0xc000003a, no filesystem), leaving ClassLibraryInfo NULL and causing a page fault. PR 9865 states that the drivers are in-tree since #9646 but the xHCI controller and USB3 root hub are in neither hardware-ID table, so setup binds no driver and an xHCI-only machine has no install media and no keyboard.

finding: The body of PR 9865 cites CORE-20821, whereas the earlier published USB3_GAP_V7.jsonl scope record listed CORE-13344 alongside PR 9865. Both JIRA issues are currently unresolved (CORE-13344 Open, CORE-20821 Untriaged, resolution null for both).
interpretation: Literal citation difference is PROVEN. That CORE-13344 and CORE-20821 share one root cause is HYPOTHETICAL only: CORE-20821 is a Skylake xHCI-only 0x7B boot failure and CORE-13344 is the general xHCI driver request. Do not merge the two issue keys in later counts without a primary link.
label: PROVEN

interpretation: All three members are unresolved at retrieval and all sit on the setup/boot side, but they touch different files and subsystems (txtsetup.sif, NTFS MFT fixup, FreeLoader hive lookup). No shared code path, symbol or commit was found. This is a research lead only, explicitly HYPOTHETICAL; it must not be recorded as an established common cause or used to justify a combined fix.
label: HYPOTHETICAL

interpretation: Weak analogy only. The subsystems share no code path and the pinned-tree WoW64 finding concerns user-mode GUI thunks, while PR 9750 concerns kernel-mode WDF bind at setup. Recorded as a HYPOTHETICAL cross-lane question for follow-up, never as a verified shared root cause.
label: HYPOTHETICAL

members.summary: ReactOS x64 doesn't have WOW64 for 32-bit applications

members.status: prerequisites present, GUI thunk stack absent

suspected_cause: Component-binding layers (WoW64 GUI thunks and WDF class-library bind) can dereference state that the corresponding loader did not establish, so incomplete prerequisite stacks surface as failures in the consumer rather than in the loader.

finding: No open FAT or boot-filesystem fix PR was identified in the bounded evidence set that could be clustered with the USB3 changes. PR 9510 is closed and unmerged; its published classification is CLOSED_UNMERGED_DESIGN_ONLY_NO_LATER_SYMBOL_CITATION_FOUND and FAT_UPSTREAM_RECHECK_V8.jsonl records LEAD_REMAINS_OPEN_CODE_STATE_UNCHANGED.
interpretation: Absence of a qualifying FAT member is a bounded-search negative result, not proof that no such PR exists anywhere. No FAT cross-lane cluster is asserted.
label: PROVEN

finding: Full 40-hex SHA token searches in GitHub issue search are unreliable for issue-to-change correlation: the pinned w64 correlation file contains a query for SHA 15c9005acb6878f5397c8fdbf9a5af59a970b8d5 whose single hit is PR 8940, an unrelated MLANG/Wine sync. Most other SHA queries returned zero items.
interpretation: Tokenisation can match unrelated text; any SHA-derived match must be confirmed by fetching the PR/issue body and testing literal substring presence before it is recorded as a correlation. No clustering in this file rests on an unconfirmed SHA search hit.
label: PROVEN

conclusion: One PROVEN shared-cause cluster (USB3 boot/setup driver binding, C1). Two explicitly HYPOTHETICAL cross-lane clusters (setup metadata validation; binding completeness). Three PROVEN negative or correction records bound the claims. No runtime test, merge or upstream submission performed; all external content treated as untrusted and all issue states re-checked from live primaries.
